issue: Does the Florida Supreme Court's 2022 decision in Somers, holding that aggravated assault cannot be based on reckless conduct, apply retroactively so that a pre-2022 Florida aggravated assault conviction does not qualify as an ACCA predicate?

sides.position: Somers does not apply retroactively under Florida law, so a pre-2022 Florida aggravated assault conviction can still qualify as an ACCA predicate
cases: United States v. Page, No. 21-3221 (7th Cir. 2024)

sides.position: Somers applies retroactively, so a pre-2022 Florida aggravated assault conviction based on reckless conduct does not qualify as an ACCA predicate
cases: Somers v. United States, 66 F.4th 890 (11th Cir. 2023)

this_court: The Seventh Circuit, as described in these excerpts, holds that Somers did not apply retroactively under Florida law. The excerpts come from a separate opinion that criticizes that approach and discusses the resulting split.
quote: Any error was "subject to reasonable dispute," Puckett, 556 U.S. at 135, as our majority opinion needed to distinguish a Florida Supreme Court decision on point and created a split with the Eleventh Circuit on an identical question.
cite: United States v. Royel Page, No. 21-3221 (7th Cir. 2024)
